mainTopic: How far a law learned through a היקש can be passed on in קדשים, by another היקש, a גזירה שוה, or a קל וחומר
overview: The גמרא first finishes showing that the פסוק about the אשם מצורע can teach that every אשם is slaughtered in the צפון, because the words 'כי כחטאת האשם' fully return it to its group. Next it asks why the same פסוק compares the אשם מצורע to both the חטאת and the עולה. רבינא answers that naming both teaches a rule: a law learned through a היקש cannot be passed on through another היקש. רבא proves the same rule from 'כאשר יורם' and the bull brought for a communal mistake. The גמרא then asks whether a law learned by היקש can teach through a גזירה שוה. A ברייתא about צרעת spreading over a garment suggests it can. רבי יוחנן limits this: it works everywhere except קדשים, and he proves it from the fact that the תורה writes 'north' by the אשם. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to discuss whether a law learned by היקש can teach through a קל וחומר, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The north verse may only be needed for the leper's guilt offering itself
steps.stepSummary: The proof works only if the general group can learn from the אשם מצורע. If neither one learns from the other, the פסוק's mention of north is needed for the אשם מצורע alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the general group can learn from it, then learning 'north' for all אשמות works well. But if we hold that the אשם מצורע does not learn from its group, and its group does not learn from it, then this פסוק is needed for its own case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a 'this works only if' setup and then raises a challenge. Under one view of דבר שיצא מן הכלל ללמד, the proof about north falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם מצורע has unique rules, so it counts as something that 'left its group.' If the group cannot learn from it, the פסוק must be telling us that the אשם מצורע itself needs the north. It then teaches nothing about other אשמות.

keyTerms.meaning: its general group (here, all guilt offerings)
learns from it
the northern part of the Temple courtyard, where the holiest offerings are slaughtered
it is needed for its own case
if we hold that...

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is the end of a sentence that began before this section ('it works well if...'). The real challenge starts at 'אלא אי סבירא לן'.

phrases.english: but its general group learns from it
(regarding the north) it works well.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: But if we hold
that it does not learn from its general group
and its general group does not learn from it
then this is needed for its own case!
phrases.notes: 'This' means the words in the פסוק saying the אשם מצורע is slaughtered where the חטאת is slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier 'this works if' setup and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that all אשמות need צפון from the אשם מצורע פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Suppose neither the אשם מצורע nor its group learns from the other. Then the פסוק's mention of north must be for the אשם מצורע alone, and it cannot teach about other אשמות.

steps.title: Once the verse returned it to its group, it returned it fully
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כי כחטאת האשם' brought the אשם מצורע back into its group completely. So the north rule is not needed for it and can teach about all אשמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק brought it back into the group, it brought it back completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק itself put the אשם מצורע back into the group of regular אשמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'like the חטאת, so is the אשם' already make the אשם מצורע follow the regular rules, including north. So the separate mention of north is extra and is free to teach that every אשם needs the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: returned it (brought it back into its group)
since / once

phrases.english: Once it returned it, it returned it.
phrases.notes: Meaning the פסוק brought it back all the way, not just partly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק itself fully restores the case to its group, so the extra words are free to teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The north words are needed for the אשם מצורע itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק already returned it to its group completely, so the north words teach about all אשמות.

steps.title: Maybe the return covers only the priestly jobs, not slaughter
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא suggests the פסוק returned the אשם מצורע to its group only for jobs that need a כהן, such as blood and burning parts. Slaughter does not need a כהן, so maybe no north is required for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said to רבינא: Say that when the פסוק returned it, that was only for placing the blood and burning the parts, which need a כהן. But slaughter, which does not need a כהן, would not need the north.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges the answer in step 2. He limits how far the 'return' goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק ends with 'לכהן,' so perhaps the return applies only to the כהן's work. If so, שחיטה, which anyone may do, was never returned. The north rule would then still be needed for the אשם מצורע itself.

keyTerms.meaning: placing the blood on the altar
the parts of the animal burned on the altar
priesthood; a job only a כהן may do
slaughtering the animal

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said to him
the son of Rav Mari, to Ravina:
Say that when the verse returned it
it was regarding placing the blood and the sacrificial parts,
which require priesthood;
but slaughter, which does not require priesthood
does not require the north!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by limiting how far the 'return' goes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק returned the אשם מצורע to its group completely
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The return may cover only priestly jobs. Then שחיטה in the north is not covered, and the north words are needed for the אשם מצורע itself.

steps.title: The extra word 'the guilt offering' means it is like all guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant to compare it to the חטאת, it could have said 'כי כחטאת הוא.' Adding 'האשם' teaches that it is like all other אשמות in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'for like the חטאת it is.' Why does it say 'like the חטאת is the אשם'? To teach that it shall be like the rest of the אשמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers מר זוטרא from the exact wording of the פסוק. The return is complete, and the step 2 answer stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'האשם' is not needed for a simple comparison. Its extra presence shows the אשם מצורע matches the other אשמות fully, slaughter in the north included. So the north words remain free to teach about all אשמות.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
let the verse say
like the rest of the guilt offerings

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'כי כחטאת האשם' fully returns the אשם מצורע to the group of regular אשמות, not only for the כהן's jobs. So the mention of north teaches that every אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say
"For like the sin offering it is";
what is "like the sin offering, the guilt offering"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:13

phrases.english: It shall be like the rest of the guilt offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects מר זוטרא's limit in step 3 and supports the answer of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The return is only for priestly jobs, so שחיטה would not need the north.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'האשם' makes it like all אשמות in every respect.

steps.title: Why compare the אשם מצורע to both the חטאת and the עולה?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares the אשם מצורע to both the חטאת and the עולה for slaughter in the north. The גמרא asks why it needs both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need to compare it to a חטאת, and why do I need to compare it to an עולה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק names two קרבנות, the חטאת and the עולה, to teach one rule about the אשם מצורע. It asks why one would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the חטאת and the עולה are slaughtered in the north. So comparing the אשם מצורע to either one should teach that it is slaughtered in the north too. Naming both looks like extra wording, and the גמרא wants to know what the extra comparison adds.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare (to link two things through a היקש)
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together in a פסוק
A sin offering
A burnt offering

phrases.english: Why do I need to compare it to a sin offering,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 14:13, which says to slaughter the אשם מצורע where the חטאת and עולה are slaughtered.

phrases.english: and why do I need to compare it to a burnt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling that the אשם מצורע must be slaughtered in the north, the גמרא asks why the פסוק compares it to two קרבנות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is gained by comparing the אשם מצורע to both the חטאת and the עולה instead of just one?

steps.title: רבינא: mentioning only the חטאת would lead to a wrong conclusion
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that if the פסוק had mentioned only the חטאת, we would think a law learned by היקש can be passed on through another היקש. The חטאת itself learns the north rule from the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Both were needed. If the פסוק had compared it only to the חטאת and not to the עולה, I would say: where does the חטאת learn its rule from? From the עולה. Then I would think that something learned by a היקש can turn around and teach by a היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers that the comparison to the עולה is needed. Without it, we would draw a wrong rule about how היקש works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת's north rule is itself learned from the עולה through a היקש. If the אשם מצורע were linked only to the חטאת, it would look as though a law learned by היקש can be passed on through another היקש. Linking it to the עולה directly blocks that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
Something whose law is learned through a היקש
Turns around and teaches (passes the law on to something else)

phrases.english: Ravina said: It was necessary;
if it had compared it to a sin offering
and not compared it to a burnt offering –

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חַטָּאת מֵהֵיכָן לָמְדָה – מֵעוֹלָה;
phrases.english: I would say: a sin offering, from where did it learn? From a burnt offering;
so a matter learned through a juxtaposition
turns around and teaches through a juxtaposition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by explaining why the comparison to the עולה is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra comparison prevents a wrong rule about היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the חטאת mentioned, we would think a law learned by היקש can teach by היקש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה is mentioned so we do not draw that wrong conclusion.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: then mention only the עולה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא asks רבינא why the פסוק did not just compare the אשם מצורע to the עולה and leave out the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב מרי, said to רבינא: Then let it compare it to the עולה and not compare it to the חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges רבינא's answer. If the עולה is the real source, the חטאת seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא explained why the עולה is needed. That explanation makes the חטאת look extra. Linking to the עולה alone would teach the north rule without any problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it compare it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:
But let it compare it to a burnt offering,
and not compare it to a sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that both comparisons are needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the עולה is needed to avoid relying on the חטאת, then the עולה alone is enough and the חטאת is extra.

steps.title: Mentioning only the עולה would also not teach the rule
steps.stepSummary: If only the עולה were mentioned, we would still think a law learned by היקש can teach by היקש. We would assume the חטאת could have done the job, and the תורה picked the עולה only because it is the main source.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would still say that something learned by a היקש turns around and teaches by a היקש. And if you ask, 'Then let it compare it to the חטאת,' I would answer that the תורה preferred to compare it to the main one and not to the secondary one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers מר זוטרא. Writing only the עולה would not prove anything, because we would explain it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the עולה mentioned, we could still think the חטאת would have worked as a source. Someone asking 'then why not use the חטאת?' would be told the תורה simply prefers the main source (the עולה) over the secondary one (the חטאת). So the choice of the עולה alone would not show that the חטאת was unable to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The main one; here, the עולה, where the north rule is stated directly
The secondary one; here, the חטאת, which learns its rule from the עולה
And if you would say
It is preferable to it

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not claim the חטאת is extra. It argues that writing only the עולה would not prove anything, because we would explain that choice as a mere preference for the main source.

phrases.english: I would say: a matter learned through a juxtaposition –
turns around and teaches through a juxtaposition;
and if you would say: let it compare it to a sin offering,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'let it compare it.'

phrases.english: it is preferable to it to compare it to the primary one
phrases.notes: The 'primary one' is the עולה. The 'secondary one' in the next line is the חטאת, which learns from it.

phrases.english: and not compare it to the secondary one;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the shorter wording would not teach the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing only the עולה would be enough to show that a law learned by היקש does not teach by היקש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Writing only the עולה could be explained as a preference for the main source, so it would prove nothing.

steps.title: Both are mentioned to teach that a law learned by היקש does not teach by היקש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names both the חטאת and the עולה to show that the חטאת alone was not enough. This teaches that דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why it compared it to the חטאת and also compared it to the עולה: to tell us that something learned by a היקש does not turn around and teach by a היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion and states the rule that the double comparison teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first names the חטאת and then still adds the עולה. This shows the חטאת could not pass on the law by itself. That proves a law learned through a היקש cannot be passed on through another היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason
That it does not turn around and teach

steps.whatToRemember: In matters of קדשים, a law learned through a היקש cannot be passed on through another היקש. The proof is that the פסוק about the אשם מצורע names both the חטאת and the עולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for how laws of קרבנות are learned. It limits how far a היקש can be extended.

phrases.english: For this reason it compared it to a sin offering
and compared it to a burnt offering –
to say that a matter learned through a juxtaposition
does not turn around and teach through a juxtaposition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 7 and fully answers the question of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The double comparison in the פסוק teaches that דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש.

steps.title: רבא brings a different source for the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the rule against a היקש-learned law teaching by היקש comes from the פסוק 'כאשר יורם משור זבח השלמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we learn it from here, as it is written: 'As it is taken off from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new source for the rule we just learned: a law learned by היקש cannot be passed on by another היקש. He only names the פסוק here; the next steps explain how it proves the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof came from the אשם מצורע being compared to both the חטאת and the עולה. רבא uses a different פסוק, about the bull of the כהן משיח, which is compared to the שלמים. This step only sets up his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning 'this is my source'
As it is taken off (the fat parts that are removed and burned on the מזבח)
The peace offering

phrases.english: Rava said: from here,
as it is written:
"As it is taken off from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:10. This is said about the חטאת bull of the כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different source for the rule concluded in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש can be learned from the פסוק 'כאשר יורם משור זבח השלמים'.

steps.title: Why is the comparison to the peace offering needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this comparison adds, since the fat parts are already listed in the bull's own section.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law is this comparison needed? If it is to teach the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, that is already written about this bull itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the comparison to the שלמים is for. The obvious answer, the fat parts, fails because the פסוק right before already lists them for this bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. Since the bull of the כהן משיח already has these parts listed in its own section, the comparison seems to add nothing. This gap sets up רבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (What does this teach us?)
The lobe (fatty membrane) of the liver, burned on the מזבח
The two kidneys, also burned on the מזבח
It is written in its own section

phrases.english: For what law?
If for the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys,
it is written in its own section!
phrases.notes: The פסוק just before (ויקרא 4:9) already lists these parts for this bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא? אִי לְיוֹתֶרֶת הַכָּבֵד וּשְׁתֵּי הַכְּלָיוֹת – בְּגוּפֵיהּ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the פסוק quoted in Step 10 adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law does the comparison of the כהן משיח's bull to the שלמים teach, if the fat parts are already written for it?

steps.title: The comparison is really for the communal bull
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is needed for פר העלם דבר של צבור, which only learns the fat parts by היקש and must then pass them on to שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תורה wants to teach the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys from the bull for a communal mistake to the goats for idol worship. But in the communal bull's own section these parts are not written; it learns them from the bull of the anointed priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the comparison is needed. The law of the fat parts has to travel from the communal bull to the goats, but the communal bull itself only got the law by היקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a chain: the כהן משיח's bull is the source, the communal bull learns from it by היקש, and the goats for idol worship learn from the communal bull. If the communal bull only has the law through a היקש, it could not pass it on by another היקש. So something more is needed, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: To teach, to pass a law from one case to another
The bull brought when the community sins by mistake based on a wrong ruling of the בית דין
The goats brought as חטאות for a communal mistake involving idol worship
The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול for his mistaken sin

phrases.english: Because it wants to teach
the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys
from the bull for a communal mistake
to the goats for idol worship;
in its own section it is not written,
phrases.notes: 'Its own section' here means the section about the communal bull.

phrases.english: and it learns it from the bull of the anointed priest;
phrases.notes: It learns this through the comparison in ויקרא 4:20, 'as he did with the bull of the sin offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by showing where the comparison is really needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the extra phrase to a different case where it is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to the שלמים seemed useless, since the כהן משיח's bull already has the fat parts listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is needed for the communal bull, which otherwise has the law only by היקש and must still pass it on to the goats.

steps.title: It counts as written directly, which proves the rule
steps.stepSummary: The extra phrase makes the law count as written in the communal bull's own section, so no היקש-learned law ends up teaching by היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why 'as it is taken off' was needed: so it will be as if it were written in the communal bull's own section, and it will not be a law learned by comparison that then teaches by comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's proof. The phrase makes the law count as written directly for the communal bull, so the communal bull can pass it on to the goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is not needed where it is written, so it is applied to the communal bull, as if written there. The תורה only needed this step because a היקש-learned law cannot teach by היקש. That is רבא's proof of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
As if it were written in its own section
Turns around and teaches (passes the law on further)

steps.whatToRemember: A law learned by היקש cannot be passed on by another היקש. So when the תורה wanted the communal bull to pass the fat parts on to the goats, it added 'כאשר יורם' so the law would count as written there directly.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'כאשר יורם' is written about the כהן משיח's bull, but its real job is for a different bull, the communal one. It is not adding anything new to the bull where it appears.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second, independent source for the rule that a היקש-learned law does not teach by היקש.

phrases.english: For this reason "as it is taken off" was needed:
so that it will be as if it were written in its own section,
phrases.notes: 'Its own section' means the communal bull's section.

phrases.english: and it will not be a law learned by comparison
that then teaches by comparison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 12 and draws רבא's proof from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The phrase 'כאשר יורם' makes the fat parts count as written for the communal bull. The תורה needed this only because דבר הלמד בהיקש אינו חוזר ומלמד בהיקש.

steps.title: רב פפא asks why not just write it plainly
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: why didn't the תורה write the fat parts directly in the communal bull's section instead of using a comparison?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Let the תורה write it in the communal bull's own section, and not make a comparison!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's proof. If the goal was for the communal bull to have the law directly, the תורה could have simply written it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the indirect phrase 'כאשר יורם' was needed so the law counts as written for the communal bull. רב פפא asks why the תורה took such a roundabout route instead of listing the parts plainly. If there is no good reason, רבא's proof becomes weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it write it
Make a comparison (use a היקש)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But let it write it in its own section,
phrases.notes: He means: write the lobe and kidneys right in the communal bull's section.

phrases.english: and not make a comparison!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וְלִיכְתְּבֵיהּ בְּגוּפֵיהּ, וְלָא נַקֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'כאשר יורם' was needed so the law counts as written for the communal bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורה wanted the law to be written directly for the communal bull, it could have written it there plainly. The roundabout comparison seems unnecessary, so it may not prove the rule.

steps.title: If the תורה only wrote it, we would learn the wrong rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: if the fat parts were only written directly in the communal bull's section with no comparison, we would think a law learned by היקש can teach by היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written it in that section itself and not made the comparison, I would have said that a law learned by היקש can go on and teach by היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins answering רב פפא's question about why the תורה did not simply write the fat parts in the communal bull's section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing it directly would remove the only case that shows the limit on היקש. With no such case, we would assume the opposite rule: a היקש-learned law can pass its law on by another היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: In its own body, meaning written directly in its own section
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two topics side by side
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Goes back and teaches, meaning it passes its law on to something else

phrases.english: If it had written it in its own section
and had not compared it
I would have said
a matter learned by a היקש
goes back and teaches by a היקש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the comparison is needed to teach a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing it directly would have been enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the comparison, we would learn the wrong rule about היקש

steps.title: Why not only compare it? Writing it directly is preferred
steps.stepSummary: רבא heads off a follow-up question: why not only use the comparison? He answers that the תורה prefers to write a law directly rather than rely only on a comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: then let the תורה only make the comparison. The answer is that the תורה prefers to write it in the section itself rather than only compare it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a possible objection to his own answer and then answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could ask: if the comparison is needed, why also write it directly? רבא says that writing a law out directly is the better way. So the תורה does both, and that leads to the conclusion in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces an expected objection)
It is preferable to it, meaning the תורה prefers
To compare, meaning to use a היקש

phrases.english: And if you would say
let it just compare it
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'let it compare.'

phrases.english: it is preferable to it
to write it in its own section
rather than only comparing it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and answers a follow-up objection to step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason the תורה prefers direct writing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the comparison is needed, the comparison alone should be enough
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה prefers to write a law directly, so it writes it and also compares

steps.title: The תורה wrote it and compared it to teach the rule
steps.stepSummary: Because the תורה both wrote the law and compared it, we learn that a law learned by היקש cannot teach by היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the תורה wrote it and also compared it: to teach that a law learned by היקש does not go on and teach by היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer and states the rule that comes out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The direct writing shows that the comparison alone could not pass the law on to the goats of עבודה זרה. That proves the general rule: a היקש-learned law cannot teach by another היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason
It wrote it and compared it
To say, meaning to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: A law learned by היקש cannot go on to teach by another היקש. רבא learns this from the communal bull, where the תורה both writes the fat parts and makes a comparison.

phrases.english: For this reason it wrote it and compared it
to say
a matter learned by a היקש
does not go back and teach by a היקש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from steps 15 and 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דבר הלמד בהיקש אין חוזר ומלמד בהיקש, proven by the communal bull being both written and compared

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid listing three ways of learning: היקש, גזירה שוה, and קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: היקש, גזירה שוה, קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists the key words of a long discussion that is about to start, so the learner can keep track.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coming discussion asks what happens when one way of learning is followed by another, such as a היקש followed by a גזירה שוה. The memory aid lists the methods that will come up.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid
Learning from the same word used in two places
Learning from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: (היקש, גזירה שוה, קל וחומר: a memory aid)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after רבא's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Memory aid listing the methods for the coming discussion

steps.title: The rule about היקש is settled from רבא or רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: a law learned by היקש cannot teach by היקש, and this is proven either by רבא or by רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A law learned by היקש does not go on and teach by היקש. We know this either from רבא's proof or from רבינא's proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what is already proven before it asks a new question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two proofs were brought for this rule, and either one is enough. With היקש-to-היקש settled, the גמרא can move on to the other combinations.

keyTerms.meaning: Either ... or

phrases.english: A matter learned by a היקש
does not go back and teach by a היקש
either from רבא or from רבינא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the rule proven in step 17 and earlier
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: היקש-to-היקש is ruled out, proven by רבא or רבינא

steps.title: Can a law learned by היקש teach by גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: a law learned by היקש cannot teach by היקש, but can it teach by גזירה שוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A law learned by היקש: what is the rule, can it teach by גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a different combination of learning methods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know היקש followed by היקש does not work. Now the גמרא asks about היקש followed by a different method, גזירה שוה, which might follow a different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it, meaning what is the rule?
A matter that is learned from somewhere else

phrases.english: A matter learned by a היקש
what is the rule, may it teach by a גזירה שוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the settled היקש-to-היקש rule to a new combination
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned by היקש can pass its law on by a גזירה שוה

steps.title: A proof begins: spreading צרעת in garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי נתן בן אבטולמוס, who learns by גזירה שוה that צרעת spreading over a whole garment is pure, comparing the words קרחת and גבחת used for garments and for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי נתן בן אבטולמוס says: How do we know that when צרעת spreads over a garment, it is pure? The words קרחת and גבחת are said about garments, and the words קרחת and גבחת are said about a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to answer its question. This step sets up the גזירה שוה, and steps 22-24 complete the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pair of words appears for garments and for a person, so the law is carried from one to the other by גזירה שוה. The גמרא will look at whether the law for a person was itself learned by היקש, which would answer the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreading of צרעת over the whole item
Pure
A bare spot, or a bald back of the head
A bare spot, or a bald forehead

phrases.english: Come and hear
Rabbi Natan ben Avtolemos says
From where do we know about spreading in garments
that it is pure?
Karachat and gabachat are said about garments
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:55

phrases.english: and karachat and gabachat are said about a person
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:42

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי נָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question in step 20
steps.raayaObject: Whether a law learned by היקש can teach by גזירה שוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי נתן בן אבטולמוס: גזירה שוה of קרחת and גבחת between garments and a person

steps.title: Finishing the comparison: a fully covered garment is pure
steps.stepSummary: Just as a person whose bald spot is fully covered with צרעת is pure, so a garment fully covered with צרעת is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as there (by the person), if the צרעת spread over all of it, it is pure. So too here (by the garment), if it spread over all of it, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the גזירה שוה of רבי נתן בן אבטולמוס. The rule of the person's head carries over to the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared words קרחת and גבחת link the garment to the person's head. So the head's rule, that full spreading is pure, moves over to the garment. This is the end result of the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: the צרעת spread over all of it
pure
just as there... so too here (the comparison formula)

phrases.english: Just as there, if it spread over all of it, it is pure,
phrases.notes: "There" is the bald spot on a person's head; "here" is the garment.

phrases.english: so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גזירה שוה started in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That a garment fully covered with צרעת is pure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה of קרחת and גבחת between the garment and the person.

steps.title: Where do we know the rule for the head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that a head fully covered with צרעת is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there (by the head), how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the head's rule. This sets up the key point of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment learned its rule from the head. Now the גמרא checks where the head got its rule from. If the head's rule came from a היקש, then the proof works.

keyTerms.meaning: and there (by the source case)
from where do we know it?

phrases.english: But there, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the case that taught step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a head fully covered with צרעת is pure.

steps.title: The head learns from the feet by היקש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'from his head to his feet' compares the head to the body. So the head's rule comes from a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'from his head to his feet.' The head is compared to the feet. Just as there, when all of it turned white and spread over all of him, he is pure, so too here, when the whole head turned white and it spread over all of it, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the head's rule was learned by היקש from the body. That rule then taught the garment by גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the chain: body → head (by היקש) → garment (by גזירה שוה). So a law learned by היקש did teach by גזירה שוה. This answers the question from step 20 with a yes.

keyTerms.meaning: from his head to his feet
was compared (by a היקש)
turned white

steps.whatToRemember: Body → head by היקש, then head → garment by גזירה שוה. So something learned by היקש can teach by גזירה שוה.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different comparisons here. Do not mix up the היקש (head to body) with the גזירה שוה (garment to head).

phrases.english: As it is written: "from his head to his feet" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:12

phrases.english: and his head is compared to his feet;
phrases.notes: Some versions say "foot" in round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected word "his feet."

phrases.english: just as there, when all of it turned white
and it spread over all of him, he is pure;
so too here, when all of it turned white
phrases.notes: Now "here" means the head.

phrases.english: and it spread over all of it, he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 and completes the proof for step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The head's rule comes from a היקש with the feet in the פסוק 'from his head to his feet'.

steps.title: Learned from learned works everywhere except קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that everywhere in the תורה we may learn from something that was itself learned, except in קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: In the whole תורה we learn something learned from something learned, except for קדשים, where we do not derive learned from learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the proof just brought. It works for צרעת, but not for the laws of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צרעת proof shows that a law from a היקש can teach by גזירה שוה. רבי יוחנן agrees in general but makes קדשים an exception. So the proof from צרעת does not settle the question for קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: learning something from a law that was itself learned
holy things, the laws of קרבנות
we derive
except for

steps.whyThisMatters: Our sugya is about קרבנות. So this exception decides how to treat chains of learning in our topic.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
In the entire Torah
we derive something learned from something learned,
except for holy offerings,
where we do not derive something learned from something learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לְמֵידִין לָמֵד מִלָּמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof of step 24 so it does not apply to קדשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learned from learned is allowed everywhere except in קדשים.

steps.title: Proof from the north side of the אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins his proof. If learned from learned worked in קדשים, the תורה would not need to write 'north' by the אשם. It could come by גזירה שוה from the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if so, let the תורה not say 'north' by the guilt offering. Let it come instead by a גזירה שוה of 'most holy' from the sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts proving his rule from the fact that the תורה writes 'north' by the אשם. The argument continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת's place of slaughter is linked to the עולה. Both אשם and חטאת are called 'most holy', so a גזירה שוה could pass the north rule to the אשם. The תורה wrote it anyway, which suggests that such a chain does not work in קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: for if it were so
in the north (side of the מזבח)
guilt offering
most holy offerings
and let it come (be learned)

phrases.english: For if it were so,
let "north" not be said about the guilt offering,
and let it be learned through a verbal analogy
of "most holy" from sin offerings;
phrases.notes: Both are called "most holy" in the תורה (ויקרא 6:18, 7:1).

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִם כֵּן לֹא יֵאָמֵר צָפוֹנָה בְּאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רבי יוחנן's rule in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That in קדשים we do not learn learned from learned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תורה writes 'north' by the אשם, even though a גזירה שוה from the חטאת could have taught it.

steps.title: What the extra verse about the אשם proves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן draws his conclusion: in קדשים, something learned by היקש cannot teach again through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this show that something learned through a היקש does not go on to teach through a גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his proof from the אשם and states what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת got its 'north' rule from a היקש to the עולה. If that learned rule could be passed on, the אשם would get 'north' from the חטאת by a גזירה שוה, and the תורה would not need to write it. Since the תורה did write it, the passing-on must not work in קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't this mean to say... (drawing a conclusion)
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two topics side by side
Learning one topic from another because the same word appears in both
Turns around and teaches (passes the rule on to something else)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rule for the whole תורה. רבי יוחנן said learning from something learned works everywhere except קדשים. This proof is only about קדשים.

phrases.english: Is this not to say
that a matter learned through a juxtaposition
phrases.notes: He means the חטאת, which learned its 'north' rule from the עולה.

phrases.english: does not turn around and teach through a verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו לְמֵימְרָא דְּדָבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ אֵין חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that started in step 26 by stating what it shows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In קדשים, something learned by היקש cannot teach again through a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Maybe the גזירה שוה fails for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תורה wrote 'north' by the אשם only because the חטאת is stronger, so the גזירה שוה could be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the reason is that the comparison can be broken: the חטאת is special, because it atones for sins that carry כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof and offers another reason the תורה had to write 'north' by the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from the חטאת to the אשם could be broken because the חטאת is more serious: it atones for sins punished by כרת, and the אשם does not. If so, the תורה wrote 'north' by the אשם for this reason, and nothing is proven about learned-from-learned.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
To break a comparison by pointing out a difference
Atones
Sins punished by כרת (being cut off)

phrases.english: But perhaps it is because one can refute:
What about a sin offering?
It is special, since it atones for sins liable to karet!
phrases.notes: The point is that the אשם doesn't do this, so it can't fully copy the חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 27 by giving another reason for the extra verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבי יוחנן's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra verse may be needed because the חטאת-to-אשם גזירה שוה can be broken by a difference, not because learned-from-learned fails.

steps.title: The extra words make the גזירה שוה unbreakable
steps.stepSummary: The words 'קדשי קדשים' are written more than needed, so the גזירה שוה cannot be broken, and רבי יוחנן's proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'most holy' are written extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback and saves רבי יוחנן's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the words used for a גזירה שוה are extra in the פסוק, the תורה clearly placed them for the comparison, so a logical difference like the כרת point cannot cancel it. That means the גזירה שוה would have worked, and the only reason the תורה still wrote 'north' by the אשם is that learned-from-learned does not work in קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level
Extra, more than needed
Are written

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה built on extra words cannot be broken by a logical difference. So רבי יוחנן's proof holds: in קדשים, a rule learned by היקש is not passed on through a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: Extra mentions of 'most holy' are written.
phrases.notes: See במדבר 18:9. Because these words are extra, the comparison they create can't be knocked down by a difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 28 and brings back the proof of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the objection doesn't apply, because a גזירה שוה from extra words cannot be broken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה from חטאת to אשם could be broken by the כרת difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words are extra, so no difference can break it. The extra verse by the אשם proves רבי יוחנן's rule.

steps.title: A rule learned by היקש can teach through a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new statement: something learned from a היקש can turn around and teach through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A matter learned from a היקש can turn around and teach through a קל וחומר...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next topic. It moves from גזירה שוה to the next way of learning, קל וחומר, and the sentence continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that in קדשים a rule learned by היקש cannot be passed on through a גזירה שוה. Now the גמרא says that passing it on through a קל וחומר does work. Its source for this comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one (if here, then surely there)
Something whose rule was itself learned from somewhere else

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix these up: in קדשים, passing the law on through a גזירה שוה does NOT work (step 27), but passing it on through a קל וחומר DOES work.

phrases.english: A matter learned from a juxtaposition
turns around and teaches through an a fortiori inference –

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד מֵהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled גזירה שוה, the גמרא moves on to the next way of learning, קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קדשים, something learned by היקש can teach through a קל וחומר (source to follow).
